issues.original: Most annual website plans fail because they start with a channel.
issues.replacement: Annual website planning often goes wrong when it starts with a channel.
issues.reason: The original makes an unsupported universal claim. This narrows it to a qualified observation without changing the structure or depth.

assessment.intent: The article gives small business owners a practical annual planning method: choose one customer bottleneck, then build a one-page website plan around it. It avoids pushing a single platform, format or channel.
assessment.specificity: Strong. It names the four bottlenecks, explains how each feels from inside a business, provides a worksheet, uses a concrete plumbing example and shows how a trade business, law firm and accommodation business would make different choices.
assessment.evidence: Adequate after the opening claim is softened. The article links to Google's people-first content guidance and Michael's Cool Runnings work without overstating the result as revenue or attributing it to one design change. It does not invent client stories, quotes or tests.
assessment.voice: The draft is mostly in Michael's voice: answer-first, practical, connected and aware of tradeoffs. The opening is now less absolute and more consistent with the rest of the article. There is no corporate padding or smug contrast.
assessment.usefulAsset: Yes. The one-page worksheet, the four-bottleneck framing and the industry differences give a busy owner enough structure to make a better annual decision without turning the post into a sales page.
